coverage_note: Arabic mixed with Latin-transliterated stretches (03:07 amalit tilha, 05:51 Lisa hom shob, 40:24-41:01 il hawa, 44:03 el nar, 45:38-46:08 el ard / nadabet, 47-49 shajar/zariya/tarab, 55-59 mufaddal). Engine: 'pantalon' 08:42 = بنطلون (not flagged); 16:55/20:05 اليوم = غيم (Amal غير شمس و يوم); 23:46 'بي البنية' = في الدنيا; 32:00 بيد = likely بيختلف/مختلف (Amal accepted); 43:06 بهدئ = بحرق; 49:10 and 49:59 شكرًا = engine for a list word (likely شجر); 09:02 'لا ما بعذر action' unclear, skipped. echo: no Arabic sound-alikes among the candidates (all real English). 05:34 تلاتة->تنتين is a fact fix, not language. 50:27 حجور/حجرات/حجار and 30:29 تلات مرة->مرات self-fixed before Amal. 1:04-1:06 English-only admin talk. Names (Palestine, Damascus, Middle East, Amsterdam = Adam/الإدام, America) not flagged.

rows.medi_said: Ayan, Ayan is sick. / خطيبتي, شوي, Ayan.
rows.why: He used masculine عيان for his fiancée; Amal echoed the feminine عيانة and he took it ('Yeah, Ayana').
rows.english: My fiancée is a bit sick.

rows.why: Amal recast his order to راسها بيوجع twice and he repeated it; his form is arguably also valid Levantine, so low.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'cough' and Amal supplied كحة.
Answering 'لسه عندكم شوب؟' he said 'hom' (them) instead of عنا (we have); Amal only re-asked the question.
rows.english: We still have a heat wave.

rows.medi_said: بين الـ، بين الـ worried. ... we are worrying.
rows.amal_said: No, you can use the adjective. Or I worry.
rows.why: English 'worried' dropped into the Arabic sentence; sheet row 'worried | Qalqaan | قلقان'. Partly a meta question; tier-3 let-pass is pre-ruled do-not-correct (AR-1933).

rows.medi_said: الـ or لا الـ نار. / لا الـ نار for fire
rows.why: He used لـ (for) after worried; Amal said 'You're worried from' and 'men', and he said من نار.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.why: He used يبدأ (begin) for a fire starting; Amal said no, another word is used (she did not give it).

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'taking care' and Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
دير بال takes على; Amal recast بالي على خطيبتي, and again at 11:45 ('بدير بالي takes على') when he repeated ديرت بالي ختيفتي - one row, the first.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: Wrong possessive ending باليك for بالك; Amal gave the command دير بالك.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / الدرس إنه، إنه تفتتلي.
rows.why: He used إنه for the relative 'that' (the lesson that you planned); should be اللي. Amal only asked what he meant.
After خلينا (let's) the verb is a bare present; he used past عملنا, Amal said نعمل, he repeated.
Non-word for 'you planned'; Amal did not understand and he switched to English; she never supplied the word.

rows.amal_said: Okay، يعني you're up to trying without.
rows.why: ra7 + bare verb needs the person prefix (أعمله); he said عمله, Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: oh my gosh, what was sky? / أنا نسيتو.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he forgot 'sky' (guessed أسف/bird first) and Amal supplied سما.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.why: Listening: he took her امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ as 'when do you watch the sky'; Amal said no, 'when does the sun go up'.

rows.medi_said: does it has to do with Azan? ... بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: أذان؟ No. أذان is the call to prayer. فجر.
rows.why: He could not find 'dawn' (tried أذان, then سجر, asked 'fajir or sajir?'); Amal supplied فجر (sheet 'dawn | el-fajer').
First-person past needs -t (نسيت); he said نسي and Amal let it pass.
تلك is Fusha 'that'; Levantine is هاي / هديك. Amal let it pass.
For 'other than' he said غير لو; Amal: 'No لو. غير.' (لو belongs to حتى لو).
غير + noun takes no el-; Amal recast غير شمس و يوم (engine يوم = غيم) twice; he then said قير شمس.
rows.english: Other than the sun and clouds.

rows.why: 'The sky at night' needs el- on سما and the noun first; Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated الـ سما بي الليل.
Didn't-know: Amal asked 'it's dark at night', he said he forgot, she supplied عتمة.
'One' follows the noun (شمس وحدة); he put it first and Amal praised the feminine without fixing the order.
noun + taani = another, agrees in gender: نجمة is feminine so تانية; Amal echoed تاني and he fixed to تانية.
Fronted object needs a pointer on the verb; Amal prompted 'point it back' and he said بشوفها.
rows.english: This is the first star I see today.

rows.medi_said: since is لـ-لـ-lessa, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He did not know 'since' (asked لسه? لا?); Amal said no and supplied من.
Feminine past of مطر is مطرت; he stumbled to 'maratat', Amal supplied مطرت, he repeated 'Matarat'.

rows.medi_said: آآ، بيد من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: 'Different from' takes عن; he used من and Amal said عن twice; he then said 'بيد and (عن) الهاوا هناك'.
rows.english: The air here is different from the air there.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... صح. آخر مرة.
rows.why: aa5er + noun = last; aa5er + el- = the end of; Amal explained and gave آخر مرة.
Amal recast his feminine past تلجات as تَلَّجَت at 36:47 (she said ممتاز at 35:27); may be only vowel length.
The subject مرة is feminine so كان must be كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he said 'feminine. كانت'.
rows.english: (The last time) was three years ago.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين ... would be for the last three years. Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي for 'ago'; Amal said no, ago is قبل, and he repeated قبل ثلاث سنين.

rows.medi_said: Il hawa aju ktir il sabah
rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟
rows.why: هوا is singular masculine; he used plural اجو; on Amal's 'what does it mean?' he said 'Oh, it's singular. Aja ktir'.
rows.english: The wind came a lot in the morning.

rows.amal_said: بهدئ. Do you know that بهدئ also means it burns?
rows.why: Amal asked the word for spicy; he only got 'به' and she supplied it (engine wrote بهدئ; 'it burns' = بحرق).

rows.medi_said: El nar, nar heret me. Does that count correct?
rows.why: The object 'me' rides on the verb as -ni; he said 'heret me' and Amal recast النار حرقتني.
The object (the floor, feminine) must ride on the verb; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said 'Nadabet ha'; she gave نظفتها.

rows.medi_said: Is it the bee? Is it bee plants? ... what's the bee?
rows.amal_said: Z-z-zبيب is raisins, I think. Is... زريعة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'plants' and Amal supplied زريعة.

rows.medi_said: Does it start with a T? / أنا ما بعرف.
rows.why: Didn't-know: Amal asked 'stones', he said he does not know; she supplied حجر.
Singular masculine الشارع cannot take قديمة; Amal recast to the plural الشوارع and he repeated الشوارع قديمة.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: 'The streets are stone' needs no verb; he built 'were made (of) stone' and Amal said just حجر: الشوارع ... حجر.
rows.english: The streets in Amsterdam are (made of) stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني; حجر تاني means another stone. Amal recast and he went back to تاني حجر.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: 'My favorite' alone is المفضل عندي (adjective with el-, owner with عندي); he said مفضل لي and Amal gave المفضل عندي.
rows.english: The second stone was my favorite.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: The adjective goes after the noun; Amal said الحجر المفضل, 'المفضل is an adjective'.
A noun with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal: 'حجري المفضل. No ال first.'

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders.
rows.why: After a definite noun the adjective needs el-: هاد الدرس المفضل عندي; Amal named the rule.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في (there is) for 'here'; Amal gave مش هون (sheet 'here | Hoan | هون') and he said 'مش هون. Okay, you're right'.
